- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits recent volatility; use 10-day moving average as baseline, then adjust ±1–2% based on sentiment skew.
